title: DR1 asks for a microchip number on horses, cats, dogs and ferrets; the frontend has no microchip field anywhere in the service.

finding.frontend: A person identifying an animal is offered at most four identifier types — passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name — and which of them appear is decided by four commodity allowlists in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:107-113. A horse, the commodity DR1 asks for a microchip first of all, is asked for two things: fe-animal-identification-horse is headed 'Horse (0101) — Equus caballus' and offers 'Passport number' and 'Horse name' and nothing else. There is no microchip field on any commodity, and no microchip obligation exists to render one: the six unit-record identifier obligations in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198 are passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name and the two free-text fallbacks.
finding.prototype: DR1 asks for a microchip on the two identifier sets a companion animal or an equine falls into. A horse (commodity code 0101) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Horse name, and a cat, dog, ferret or other live mammal (all commodity code 01061900) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Tattoo — app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-19. Microchip is the first field on both panels, so it is the identifier DR1 puts in front of the person first.
finding.difference: Add a microchip identifier to the per-animal record: a new unit-record obligation alongside the existing five in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js, a MICROCHIP_COMMODITIES allowlist holding Horse, Cat and Dog in the stub's picker-name vocabulary, a label in the identification copy block, and the new obligation id added to the unit record's requires.anyOfIds so a microchip on its own satisfies the at-least-one-identifier rule. Adding it also widens the derived union behind specificIdentifierWhitelists, which is what stops a microchip-only commodity falling through to the free-text fallback fields.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a microchip field rendered on the frontend's horse, cat or dog identification panel, or finding that DR1's horse and 01061900 identifier sets do not include a Microchip entry.
finding.correction: The finding stands. The carried-over claim it rests on — that app/data/commodity-identifiers.js is release-agnostic, so a set written for DR2.1 also describes DR1 — was checked at the root mount and holds. The identification page resolves a species' fields through getIdentifierFieldsForSpecies (app/routes.js:1458-1471), which calls getIdentifiersForCommodityCode on the commodity's code and returns whatever that file holds; there is no release test anywhere on that path, no equivalent of the isDesignRelease21SessionData filter that getSearchCommodities applies to the commodity catalogue itself (app/routes.js:61-73), and the one release-conditional thing in the file — the germinal-product sets under 05119985 and 05111000 — is unreachable in DR1 because those commodities are never offered. Horse 0101 and companion-animal 01061900 are both in DR1's catalogue and both carry Microchip. Two things are read from source rather than seen: neither captured page holds a horse or a companion animal, so nobody has photographed a DR1 microchip field, and the claim that Microchip is 'the first field on both panels' is a reading of the template loop over the data order rather than an observation. Medium confidence is the right band, and the named control will not resolve to a crop on either captured screen. SECOND PASS, after the state was captured: a horse line was driven and shot as fe-animal-identification-horse after this finding was written, and it settles the frontend half by absence. The panel a person meets when identifying a horse holds exactly two boxes, 'Passport number' and 'Horse name', where DR1's horse set is Microchip, Passport and Horse name — so the missing field is now missing in a picture, on the one commodity in the frontend's catalogue where DR1 asks for it first. The falsifier's frontend limb was put to the only test that could fire and did not. Confidence raised to high. Two things stay true from the first pass and should not be read as settled by the capture. DR1's microchip panel is still unphotographed — neither DR1 screen holds a horse or a companion animal — so the prototype half remains a read of app/data/commodity-identifiers.js, and the claim that Microchip is the first field on both DR1 panels remains a reading of the template loop over the data order. And the named control still resolves on no captured screen at all, on either side: it is absent from the frontend by definition and absent from DR1's cattle panel by data. The crop will not render and the report will fall back to a whole-page shot of fe-animal-identification-horse, which is the right page to look at even so, because what it shows is the gap. THIRD PASS, on whether any captured screen could carry the control: none can, and the control is kept named so the report keeps saying so. On the frontend no state can ever show a microchip field, on any commodity, because no such field exists — that absence is the finding, and fe-animal-identification-horse is the page where it bites hardest, so that whole-page shot is this finding's frontend evidence and should be read as evidence of an absence rather than as a failed crop. On DR1 the control would resolve on an identification page driven to commodity 0101 (horse) or 01061900 (cat, dog, ferret or other live mammal), where app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-19 puts Microchip first on the panel. The corpus does not hold that state: dr1-animal-identification-details was captured on a cattle line and its two boxes are `identifiers[cattle-11-syncerus-spp][ear-tag]` and `identifiers[cattle-11-syncerus-spp][passport]`, and cattle have no microchip in DR1's own data. The string 'Microchip' occurs in no captured HTML on either side. Capturing the DR1 horse panel would settle the prototype half of this finding in a picture and is the one thing that would; it needs a change to the prototype's own capture spec, which is outside this corpus's findings.

relatedTo.why: the same per-commodity identifier sets; both are corrections to which identifier types a commodity is asked for
